Geographic IDs & count precision

The atlas is a nine-county window, not a claim that one boundary is the “real” city. A functional employment catchment depends on whose connections you count, and how many you want it to contain.

Data, method & limits+

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics, 2023 JT01, release 8.4, data vintage 20251202_1657, accessed September 29, 2026. Original analysis and interface; no Census endorsement. Public aggregate data, credited under the Census open-data policy.

Which jobs?

Primary means a person’s highest-earning job in the covered frame. The Q2 “beginning of quarter” frame requires positive earnings in Q1 and Q2. Resident jobholders here are estimated primary-job counts grouped by home, not a city’s population. The frame includes unemployment-insurance-covered employment and available OPM federal jobs. Self-employment, informal employment, military service and some federal agencies/occupations are excluded. Data overview · Federal coverage.

Which relationships?

California’s main file covers homes and workplaces in California. Its auxiliary file covers California workplaces with homes elsewhere. To retain outbound links, this page also reads the auxiliary files of all 48 other available workplace states. Alaska and Michigan workplaces are unavailable for 2023; their residents can appear with jobs elsewhere. Territories are outside this frame. All percentages use this available-job universe, not complete U.S. employment.

What is not measured?

LODES combines administrative records with imputation, synthetic residential allocation and disclosure-avoidance noise. It does not identify people or observe routes, modes, commute time, office attendance or daily journeys. Remote work and employer address assignments matter. Long-distance pairs cannot be interpreted as daily travel. Small differences are not tested for statistical significance. See the Census comparison of ACS and LODES and review of cross-state flows.

How geography is assigned

The release maps 2020 census blocks to higher geography from 2024 TIGER. Counts use the actual California crosswalk’s county, place and tract fields, never a name match or a derived tract prefix. Each Bay node is a county × place portion; “CDP” is a statistical place, not an incorporated city. County remainders contain blocks outside named places. Tract views are the portion of a current tract assigned to that place. Generalized 2024 Census map outlines are clipped by county and simplified for display; they do not determine counts.

What the atlas contains

Other California counties are grouped by county; other states by state. Those external buckets are coarser than Bay places. Their displayed counts describe links with the chosen Bay home area, not all employment in those external areas. Unavailable destinations use “N/A”; a released zero uses “0.” The “both elsewhere” ledger cell is outside its comparison, not zero.

What changing a boundary does

For a selected boundary: resident jobs = internal + home-inside/work-outside; workplace jobs = internal + home-outside/work-inside. Adding an area makes its links with the original boundary internal and brings its other links into scope. Counts and endpoints are preserved. Whole-boundary percentages acquire a new resident denominator. This is reclassification, not a change in jobs, transport or emissions.

The opening is the incorporated Bay place with at least 10,000 resident jobholders and the closest workplace/resident ratio in this release. Only total-job column S000 is displayed. Age, earnings and industry columns are separate marginal counts; they are not crossed into individual profiles. No comparison across years is made. Rounded story numbers avoid false precision; exact released integers are available for auditing arithmetic, not as a census of identifiable people.

Every OD/crosswalk download was checked against its official decompressed-file SHA-256. Independent raw-data aggregation reproduces every embedded place and tract link. LODES 8.4 technical specification · Explore the Census OnTheMap tool.
